newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close higher, lifted by STET surge.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close higher, lifted by STET surge.

text.p: Milan shares ended higher on Tuesday driven by the sharp rise in STET shares which were suspended at the 10 percent limit up ceiling minutes before the bourse closed, while the firmer trend to bonds supported gains.

State-controlled telecoms holding group STET continued to show strong gains after the shares rose rapidly late Monday when the Italian Treasury said it planned to merge STET with Telecom Italia. STET share were last quoted up 9.89 percent at 6,235 percent after hitting a day's high of 6,240 lire.
The all-share Mibtel index ended up 1.9 percent at 10,141 and the Mib30 index up 2.28 percent at 15,255 lire.

Dealers said that STET would lose its holding company status after a merger with Telecom Italia, and hence its shares would be more attractive to international investors when the STET privatisation gets underway in late 1997.
After Monday's sharp losses, Telecom Italia shares steadied, and ended up 0.3 percent at 3,331 lire.

Among other shares, Olivetti also gained adding 3.55 percent to 495.7 lire following on from Monday's gains which were helped by Friday's news of the sale of a stake in Omnitel to Germany's telecoms and engineering group Mannesmann.
In the industrial sector, Fiat added 2.02 percent to 4,602 lire with Pirelli up 2.46 percent to 2,748 lire and Montedison 0.76 percent firmer at 1,064 lire.
